candidates.name: depth5_delta_60s
candidates.mechanism: Depth delta: the trailing-60s CHANGE in 5-level depth imbalance (bid-ask)/(bid+ask), not its level. A book whose bid-side depth stock is actively growing relative to the ask side is experiencing net limit-order inflow on the bid - latent demand building up before it shows up in trades. The level of imbalance (wdi) is crowded and slow; the delta captures the flow INTO the deeper book and should decorrelate from the level by construction (differencing removes the persistent state), targeting the digest's explicitly unexplored 'depth delta' dimension.
candidates.inspiration: Digest iter-000 opportunity map: 'Depth-side unexplored: resiliency, depth delta, queue position, large-order depth share'; cross-family mutation away from the depth mega-family has higher marginal value (rho 0.69 within family); Cao-Hansch-Wang (2009) information content of the book's depth dynamics.
candidates.verdict_detail: Gate ADMIT at 15s: OOS t=9.68 >= Harvey-Liu 3.869, BHY-FDR pass, OOS IC 0.134 = 8.5x permutation floor, 22/22 days positive. 30s/60s variants miss the pre-registered screen retention budget (0.497/0.44 < 0.5) despite OOS t 9.1/10.4 -- NOT forwarded, no post-hoc relaxation; re-screen with longer OOS in iter-002.

candidates.name: flow_divergence_300s
candidates.mechanism: Absorption / stealth limit flow: the trailing-300s z-score of OFI (order-book-delta flow: limit placement/pull at the touch) minus the z-score of executed trade imbalance. Positive divergence means the book is being built on the bid side relative to what aggressive trades justify - passive buyers absorbing sell aggression (iceberg/stealth accumulation); negative divergence is the mirror. The limit-flow component dominates for next-move prediction (CKS: OFI R2 > signed volume), and disagreement between executed and book-building flow flags informed traders hiding in the book, so the divergence direction should carry into 15s-300s returns.
candidates.inspiration: Digest iter-000: ofi vs trade_imbalance rho=0.49 and 'the ORDER-BOOK-DELTA component of OFI not in trade imbalance is worth isolating'; Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov (2014) OFI dominates signed volume; absorption via iceberg orders (Buti & Rindi 2013, undisplayed liquidity).
candidates.verdict_detail: Gate ADMIT at 15s: OOS t=4.00 >= 3.869 (3% margin), BHY-FDR pass, OOS IC 0.033 = 1.9x floor, win rate 20/22. 30s fails the Stage-1 hurdle (t=2.51 < 3.869) though it clears floor and FDR -- honest Stage-1 negative. Mega-family-orthogonal (rho < 0.05 vs wdi/oir/microprice).

candidates.name: queue_refill_asym_300s
candidates.mechanism: Coarse resiliency / queue-refill asymmetry: after a top-of-book depth depletion step on one side, how much depth is back 15s later, averaged over depletion events in the trailing 300s, bid vs ask, normalized by average top-of-book size. A bid queue that refills faster than the ask queue means patient buy-side liquidity keeps re-arming: downward probes get absorbed and the next move is biased up (fast refill = temporary impact = mean reversion of the depleting move; slow/partial refill = informed consumption = continuation). This is a genuine DYNAMICS quantity - refill speed - orthogonal to depth-imbalance LEVELS (the oir/wdi family).
candidates.inspiration: Digest iter-000: 'arrival/cancel dynamics only testable via snapshot-delta reconstruction' on SSE and the opportunity map lists resiliency as unexplored depth-side; Obizhaeva & Wang (2013) resiliency after large trades; Foucault-Kadan-Kandel (2005) limit order book replenishment.
candidates.verdict_detail: Screen FAIL on retention alone (0.32 < 0.5 at 15s; OOS t=4.10 still significant, no sign flip): resiliency information exists on 588000 but is regime-dependent (strong Jul-Aug, weak Sep). iter-002: condition on rv/iopv regime or retest with more months.

candidates.name: ti_ewm_state_300s
candidates.mechanism: Flow-accumulation state variable: an exponentially-weighted running integral of signed aggressive trade imbalance with ~150s half-life. Meta-orders (institutional execution, arbitrage baskets vs IOPV) arrive over minutes, so the integrated imbalance of executed aggressor flow is a persistent pressure/information state, not a 60s impulse. High positive state = sustained net buying aggression accumulated over the last several minutes -> continuation expected at 60-300s horizons, where the library's fixed 60s windows have already decayed to their tails.
candidates.inspiration: Digest iter-000: '300s HORIZON = WEAKEST AND MOST OPEN ... every library flow factor uses a 60s lookback, so 300s only sees decay tails. Proposals with 2-5 min state variables (flow accumulation) directly target this gap'; meta-order propagation and square-root impact (Bouchaud-Gefen-Potters-Wyart 2004, G(t) ~ t^-1/2).
candidates.verdict_detail: No horizon passed screen; rank-corr 0.957 with ti_accum_300s -> merged into the smoothed-trade-imbalance duplicate cluster (kept representative: ti_accum_300s). Slow EWMA accumulation does NOT extend flow to 300s on 588000; OOS-only negative 900s effect (t=-2.48) routed to the long/short decomposition (task #86).

candidates.name: ti_ewm_accel_120s
candidates.mechanism: Aggressive-flow acceleration: fast EWMA (15s half-life) minus slow EWMA (60s half-life) of signed trade imbalance - a MACD of aggressor flow. The LEVEL of imbalance says where flow has been; the acceleration says where it is turning. A burst of one-sided aggression (sweeping several book levels within seconds) precedes short-horizon continuation (queue depletion cascades), while a deceleration of previously strong flow precedes stalls/reversion. Because it is a difference of two backward filters of the same series it is nearly orthogonal to the flow LEVEL factors by construction.
candidates.inspiration: Digest iter-000: flow signals die by 900s and peak at 15s - the fresh information in flow is its CHANGE, not its level; momentum-trigger logic in order-flow bursts (Cartea-Jaimungal-Penalva 2015, ch.8 aggressive-order dynamics).
candidates.verdict_detail: Double failure: rank-corr 0.739 vs its own source column trade_imbalance_60s (fails the 0.7 novelty bar) -- fast-minus-slow EWMA of an already-windowed series tracks its level; plus OOS t <= 1.5 at every horizon. Do not retry flow-MACD on windowed inputs; differentiate raw 3s flow deltas instead.

candidates.name: iopv_premium_mom
candidates.mechanism: IOPV premium momentum: the exchange IOPV refreshes on <=15s steps while the ETF trades continuously, so the premium's 30s rate of change is distinct from its level. A widening premium (ETF running ahead of fair value) flags continuation pressure; a narrowing premium flags active arbitrage pull-back. This is the lead-lag between basket fair value and ETF price captured as premium velocity, not premium level.
candidates.inspiration: digest: 'IOPV dimension is thin (1 factor, level only); premium momentum/delta ... unexplored and orthogonal to the depth mega-family' (max |rho| of iopv_premium vs all others = 0.23); docs/knowledge/02 ETF lead-lag section (basket/fair-value pulls the ETF with seconds-to-minutes lag).
candidates.verdict_detail: Screen PASS at 900s (retention 0.56) but Stage-1 gate rejects: one-sided hurdle blocks the negative sign (t=-3.00) and |OOS IC| 0.0095 sits BELOW the 0.0179 permutation floor (IS 0.0171 is above). Genuinely new vs parent (rho 0.37). Route: task #86 long/short decomposition, batched with parent iopv_premium.

candidates.name: prem_x_ofi
candidates.mechanism: Premium x order-flow interaction: premium mean-reversion is driven by AP creation/redemption arbitrage, but its speed depends on the prevailing order flow. When the ETF is at a premium AND net order flow is selling, the forces reinforce reversion (stronger predicted down-move); when flow opposes the premium, reversion is delayed. The product of the causally z-scored premium and OFI isolates this conditional-reversion channel rather than either signal alone.
candidates.inspiration: digest: 'premium x order-flow interaction ... orthogonal to the depth mega-family'; iopv_premium is the strongest mean-reversion signal (|t|=7.9) and ofi_60s the strongest flow signal, yet their INTERACTION is unexplored and sits in a different info dimension.
candidates.verdict_detail: Interaction dimension is real (max rho 0.093 vs library) but information-free on 588000: no IS signal at any horizon (|t| <= 1.28, magnitudes below the permutation floor) and IS->OOS sign flips at 15/30/60s. AP arbitrage acts on the premium itself; reversion timing is not gated by local ETF order flow.

candidates.name: prem_x_wdi
candidates.mechanism: Premium x depth-imbalance interaction: a positive premium means the ETF is rich vs fair value (arbitrage pressure downward), but the book's depth imbalance decides how fast reversion lands. A premium paired with a bid-heavy book (high wdi) is being propped up and reverts slowly; paired with an ask-heavy book it snaps back fast. The product of causally z-scored premium and wdi captures this conditional-reversion timing, a cross-family interaction.
candidates.inspiration: digest: wdi is the cost-friendly champion (slowest decay, half-life 900s) and iopv_premium the most independent signal (max |rho|=0.23); cross-family mutation (IOPV x depth) has 'far higher marginal value than more imbalance variants'.
candidates.verdict_detail: Cleanest null of the iteration: max |t| = 0.93 across all 10 IS/OOS horizon blocks. Fully orthogonal (max rho 0.037) but zero support for the conditional-reversion-timing hypothesis.

candidates.name: vol_adj_slope
candidates.mechanism: Volatility-adjusted book slope: a steep order book partly just encodes that recent volatility has been low (book_slope corr ~0.60 with rv_300s). A causal trailing-window regression removes the vol-explained component, leaving the slope deviation NOT explained by recent realized vol -- the pure book-shape / support-resistance concentration signal that carries minutes-scale (300s+) predictive content, targeting the open 300s gap.
candidates.inspiration: digest: 'book_slope correlated with rv_300s (rho=0.60): on 588000 slope partly just encodes recent volatility; a vol-adjusted slope is an obvious mutation' + '300s horizon = weakest and most open'.
candidates.verdict_detail: Residualization structurally succeeded (rho 0.325 vs book_slope, 0.127 vs rv_300s) but residual predictive content is at the noise floor; 15/30s OOS collapse (retention 0.28/0.36). Most of the minutes-scale information in book_slope WAS the stripped vol component. The 300s exploitable gap remains open.

candidates.name: depth_resiliency
candidates.mechanism: Depth resiliency: market makers with quoting obligations replenish the book after trades consume it. The 60s change in TOTAL depth (bid+ask), normalized by its trailing 300s level, is a snapshot resiliency proxy. Rising total depth = active replenishment, so recent shocks are transient (mean reversion); falling total depth = liquidity withdrawal, so shocks are informative (continuation). Built from total depth, NOT bid-vs-ask imbalance, so it sits in a different dimension from the wdi/oir/microprice mega-family.
candidates.inspiration: digest: 'Depth-side unexplored: resiliency, depth delta, queue position, large-order depth share'; Foucault-Kadan-Kandel (2005) and Obizhaeva-Wang (2013) resiliency -> reversal-vs-continuation over 1-5 minutes (targets the open 300s horizon).
candidates.verdict_detail: Orthogonal (max rho 0.072) but UNCONDITIONAL total-depth change on the 3s grid is dominated by MM quote updates with no directional content: 15/30s evaporate OOS (retention 0.35/0.19); 300s OOS t=-3.04 sign-flips from IS t=-0.23 (regime artifact). Event-conditioned resiliency remains testable as a different prototype later.

candidates.name: session_clock
candidates.mechanism: Intraday session-clock seasonality: maps each snapshot to its elapsed continuous-trading time in [0,1] (09:30->0, 11:30->0.5, 13:00->0.5, 15:00->1), skipping the lunch break. This is the clean test of whether 588000 short-horizon returns carry any deterministic time-of-day drift (open/close effects, lunch-resumption, U-shape positioning). Pure calendar/time features have no microstructure state of their own, so a null result is informative: seasonality must enter as CONDITIONING of other signals, not as a standalone directional factor.
candidates.inspiration: digest: 'GAP dimension = time_of_day (ts_ms unused by all 12 factors - open/close auctions, lunch-break boundary, U-shape vol normalization, time-conditioning)'; docs/knowledge/02 section 6 intraday seasonality (U-shape volume/vol, 13:00 second open).
candidates.verdict_detail: Pre-registered negative: pure monotonic time-of-day carries no exploitable drift on 588000 (max |t| 2.03 IS, below the permutation floor at short horizons; no OOS significance despite consistent sign and retention 0.66-0.83). Seasonality should enter as CONDITIONING of other signals, not as an alpha column. Caveat: a monotonic clock is blind to non-monotonic U-shape patterns.

candidates.name: ti_accum_300s
candidates.mechanism: Persistence of signed-volume asymmetry over minutes: the library trade_imbalance_60s is a 60s snapshot of directional flow that decays to zero IC by 300-900s, but informed flow is worked into price over MANY minutes as one-sided meta-orders (Kyle 1985), and the price impact of executed flow decays only as a power law (~t^-1/2, Bouchaud et al. 2004). A trailing 300s average of signed trade imbalance is an ACCUMULATION state variable: it keeps the direction of persistent one-sided flow while averaging out idiosyncratic bursts, matching the minutes-scale memory a 60s window cannot see. Targets the 300s/900s horizon gap.
candidates.inspiration: Digest iter-000: 'FLOW SIGNALS DIE BY 900s ... long-horizon flow constructs need accumulation/state variables instead of 60s windows'; 300s horizon = 0/12 stage1 passes, the biggest open gap. Accumulation logic analogous to VPIN's bucketed signed-volume sums (Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara 2012) applied to the exchange-aggressor-flagged imbalance; impact power-law tail per Bouchaud, Gefen, Potters & Wyart (2004).
candidates.verdict_detail: 0/5 horizons passed screen (<=60s edge collapses OOS, retention 0.13-0.60; 900s negative IC lacks IS support, IS t=-1.42). Kept as representative of the merged duplicate cluster {ti_accum_300s, ti_ewm_state_300s rho 0.957, dd_flow_300s rho 0.894}. Simple signed-flow accumulation adds no stable information beyond the 60s base on 588000.

candidates.name: ofi_accum_300s
candidates.mechanism: Accumulated order-book-delta pressure over minutes: the engine's ofi_60s is the Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov best-quote OFI (limit-order placements, pulls AND trades) normalized by mean best depth, and its IC decays from 0.093@15s to ~0 by 900s. But OFI's price impact relaxes only as a power law, so successive minutes of net-positive queue building leave residual pressure that a 60s window forgets. Averaging OFI over 300s yields a minutes-scale accumulation state distinct from both trade-flow accumulation (digest rho(ofi, trade_imbalance) = 0.49, only partial overlap) and static book levels (wdi/oir). Targets 300s/900s.
candidates.inspiration: Digest iter-000: 'the ORDER-BOOK-DELTA component of OFI not in trade imbalance is worth isolating'; Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (2014) OFI linear impact; Bouchaud et al. (2004) propagator t^-1/2 tail justifies multi-minute integration of flow; 300s horizon is the weakest-and-most-open gap (mean |IC| 0.064, 0/12 stage1 passes).
candidates.verdict_detail: Screen PASS at 900s (IS -0.070 t=-2.87; OOS -0.068 t=-2.15; retention 0.98) but Stage-1 rejects: negative sign + |t| below the Harvey-Liu hurdle. 15-minute REVERSAL signal (sustained net buying predicts downward drift), OOS IC 3.7x floor, genuinely distinct from instantaneous ofi_60s (rho 0.265). Route: task #86, sign-flipped re-test. Note rho 0.75 with rv_asym_300s.

candidates.name: rv_asym_300s
candidates.mechanism: Directional accumulation of volatility over minutes: the library rv_60s/rv_300s keep only the MAGNITUDE of realized variance, but volatility clusters with a sign signature -- runs of downside jumps (stop cascades, distressed/inventory selling) vs upside jumps (short covering, news absorption). The trailing-300s realized semivariance asymmetry (up-RV minus down-RV over total) is a signed vol-state: asymmetric vol regimes persist (vol-of-vol clustering) and carry directional drift into the next minutes, whereas pure vol level is direction-free. Targets 300s/900s, exactly where the unsigned rv_60s is the only library factor whose |IC| RISES with horizon.
candidates.inspiration: Realized semivariance and good/bad volatility: Barndorff-Nielsen, Kinnebrock & Shephard (2010), Patton & Sheppard (2015, REStat). Digest iter-000: rv_60s |IC| rises monotonically 0.014@15s -> 0.047@900s (vol information lives in the minutes window) but the library keeps it unsigned; vol-of-vol/second-moment accumulation is the lens item, made directional via semivariance asymmetry (an unsigned vol-of-vol level was rejected ex ante as direction-symmetric and not worth a trial-ledger entry).
candidates.verdict_detail: Screen PASS at 900s with the strongest IS evidence of the batch (IS -0.084 t=-3.69; OOS -0.058 t=-2.07; retention 0.69) but Stage-1 rejects on negative sign + |t| < hurdle. Signed-vol dimension is genuinely new (rho 0.036 vs rv_60s/rv_300s): upside-dominated vol predicts LOWER 15-min returns (mean reversion after directional jump runs). Route: task #86. Note rho 0.75 with ofi_accum_300s -- pick one or portfolio-dedup if both revive.

candidates.name: dd_flow_300s
candidates.mechanism: Drawdown-state conditioning of accumulated flow: the distance of mid from its running intraday high measures trapped-long / stop-loss potential energy. Directional flow delivered WHILE the instrument sits deep below its day-high is more informative: distressed selling, stop cascades and opportunistic absorption all concentrate in that state, so the same accumulated imbalance carries different implications at the high vs in the drawdown. value = (trailing-300s mean trade imbalance) x (-drawdown), amplifying accumulated flow by drawdown depth. Neither component alone (imbalance accumulation, price position) captures the interaction. Whether the sign of IC comes out continuation (selling begets selling) or absorption (dip-buying reverses) is the empirical question; the screen is two-sided.
candidates.inspiration: Lens item 'drawdown-from-day-open interactions'; digest iter-000 coverage GAP: price-position/time-of-day information unused by all 12 library factors; intraday-extreme anchoring (George & Hwang 2004) adapted to the running day-high; stop-cascade / distress continuation vs absorption is a standard minutes-scale regime mechanism.
candidates.verdict_detail: 0/5 horizons: short-horizon IS t up to 4.6 evaporates OOS (retention 0.03-0.41, IS-only regime); 300/900s signs flip with no IS support (OOS-only apparition). Drawdown x flow interaction is regime-specific to Jul-Aug 2025; rank-corr 0.894 with ti_accum_300s shows the drawdown modulation adds almost no rank information. Merged into the ti_accum cluster.

candidates.name: wdi_mom_90s
candidates.mechanism: Momentum of book state: the LIBRARY tests only the LEVEL of weighted depth imbalance (wdi), the slowest-decaying signal on 588000 (half-life 900s). A book that is actively BUILDING one-sided depth over the last ~90 seconds is a different state from one that is statically lopsided: the delta separates active accumulation of book pressure (queue being rebuilt on one side) from stale imbalance that market makers have already priced. Rising wdi momentum should precede continued mid drift at 60-300s horizons, adding the time-derivative dimension of the depth family that the level-only library lacks.
candidates.inspiration: Digest iter-000: wdi is the cost-friendly champion with the slowest decay (still IC 0.134/t=4.4 at 900s); opportunity map lists depth DELTA as unexplored; queue-imbalance changes as the coarse direction of net queue replenishment (cf. Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov 2014 OFI book-event decomposition); lens item 'momentum-in-book-state'.
candidates.verdict_detail: Retention-ONLY screen failure (0.22-0.45 < 0.5 at all horizons) despite IS|t| 5.4-9.8 and OOS|t| 2.7-11.5 at ALL 5 horizons, same positive sign everywhere, OOS t EXCEEDING IS t at 15-60s (no overfit signature); OOS IC 0.056-0.065 is library-passing magnitude. Pre-registered gate upheld, NO post-hoc tuning -- but this is the strongest OOS evidence of the batch: MUST be re-examined with a longer OOS in iter-002 and cross-sectionally at multi-asset scale-up. Independent of depth5_delta_60s (rho 0.369).

candidates.name: large_trade_share_60s
candidates.mechanism: Trade-size conditioning: share of trailing-60s aggressive volume carried by large prints. Large trades carry more information (urgent informed flow splits less); the size DISTRIBUTION of flow - not just its signed sum - should condition continuation/reversal. Complements ofi/ti which are size-blind sums.
candidates.info_set: Materialized 2026-08-05 (#137): engine column large_trade_share_60s computed from per-trade Volume + TrdBSFlag, replayed over all 66 days (42-col panel).
candidates.inspiration: Lens mandate 'trade-size conditioning'; digest opportunity map 'large-order depth share' unexplored; Kyle (1985); Bouchaud et al. (2004) square-root meta-order impact.
candidates.detail: iter-002, eval v2 (IC-primary gate, cost 3bp/side, OOS = 20250924-0930, 5 days, train 20250701-0923): screened as identity prototype large_trade_share_level (spec c8f7602). rejected_duplicate flag is STRUCTURAL (identity of the source column, corr 1.0 vs PANEL_FACTORS universe) and not informative; the IC rows are the evidence: |IC| <= 0.025 with |t| <= 1.90 at ALL horizons 15/30/60/300/900s; the borderline 300/900s IS t (-1.65/-1.90) flips sign OOS (no retention). Head stats tau=5% OOS: long gross +0.5/+0.9/+1.1bp at 15/30/60s (net -5.5/-5.1/-5.0bp after 6bp RT), 300/900s long gross +3.5/+1.2bp with short gross -7.0/-6.7bp but IC gate fails (noise). VERDICT: the LEVEL of the large-trade share does not predict 588000 mid returns at any horizon; mechanism may still work as a CONDITIONING variable (interactions, e.g. flow x large-share) -- see iter-003.

candidates.name: trade_arrival_burst
candidates.mechanism: Trade-arrival bursts (Hawkes self-excitation / ACD): information events cluster, so a burst in trade-arrival rate relative to its trailing baseline flags the start of an information episode that unfolds over minutes (300/900s signal). Requires actual trade counts or inter-trade durations.
candidates.info_set: Materialized 2026-08-05 (#137): n_trades_60s engine column; prototype = z-score of 300s arrival intensity (rolling mean of n_trades_60s, FAST=100 rows) vs trailing-1800s baseline (BASE=600 rows), spec b9592ff.
candidates.inspiration: Engle & Russell (1998) ACD; Hawkes self-excitation; digest: arrival/cancel dynamics only testable on SZSE or via snapshot-delta reconstruction.
candidates.detail: iter-002, eval v2 (IC-primary gate, cost 3bp/side, OOS = 20250924-0930, 5 days, train 20250701-0923): run + screen over all 66 days, dedup universe = PANEL_FACTORS, max |corr| 0.320 (novel, not a duplicate). FAIL at ALL horizons 15/30/60/300/900s: |IC| <= 0.012 with |t| <= 0.77 IS and <= 1.18 OOS; the only notable cell (OOS 900s IC -0.093, t -1.18) flips sign vs IS (no retention). Head stats tau=5% OOS: long gross +0.4/+0.6/+1.0bp at 15/30/60s (net -5.6/-5.4/-5.0bp after 6bp RT), short gross ~0; 300/900s both heads negative. VERDICT: direction-free arrival INTENSITY (burst z-score) carries no rank information about 588000 mid returns at any horizon; signed-arrival or conditional variants (burst x concurrent direction) remain untested -- see iter-003.

eval_v2_rescreen_2026_08_05.trigger: Two infrastructure changes invalidated all pre-2026-08-05 screen numbers: (1) #141 fixed a purged_day_splits last-fold residual-chunk bug (old OOS fold composition was wrong); (2) eval-v2 directive replaced the Harvey-Liu hurdle gate with an IC-primary gate. All 18 registered prototypes re-screened from scratch under v2; this block is the authoritative baseline for future iterations.

gate.retention_sign_rule: retention = |OOS IC|/|IS IC| AND requires same IS/OOS sign; sign flip fails retention regardless of ratio

eval_v2_rescreen_2026_08_05.head_stats_semantics: Computed on OOS block only (5 days). Per-date quantiles of factor value: long head = rows >= q(1-tau), short head = rows <= q(tau). long_gross_bps = mean(fwd_mid_ret of top)*1e4; short_gross_bps = -mean(fwd_mid_ret of bottom)*1e4 (SIGN-FLIPPED bottom leg: compare long_gross against -short_gross = raw bottom mean to check consistency with IC sign). net = gross - 6bp round trip. No IC-sign adjustment. Same-sign legs = OOS-week drift or time-of-day concentration, not an anomaly. tau=1% legs are ~40 rows/day, noise-dominated at 300/900s (e.g. wdi_mom_90s positive IC yet tau1%/tau5% legs look inverted; only tau10% agrees). DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, never gates admission.

summary.observation: 4 of 6 passes are at 900s; only flow_divergence_300s holds 15-60s. Retention, not OOS significance, is the dominant short-horizon killer: depth5_delta_60s / wdi_mom_90s / queue_refill_asym_300s all show OOS |t| 3-11 at 15-60s yet fail retention 0.08-0.47.

dedup_within_batch.cluster_caveat: dd_flow_300s x ti_accum_300s rho 0.894 and x ti_ewm_state_300s rho 0.859 (FAIL members of the same flow-accumulator cluster); rv_asym_300s x ofi_accum_300s rho 0.750. Keep at most one representative per cluster in future batches.
dedup_within_batch.session_clock_note: max rho 0.252 (vs trade_arrival_burst), else <= 0.05: orthogonal time-of-day dimension.

verdicts.name: depth5_delta_60s
verdicts.note: Genuinely strong signal that decays too fast for the retention bar at 15-300s (OOS t 10.55 at 15s yet retention 0.470). 900s head legs noise-dominated at tau1%/5%; tau10% consistent with positive IC. Monitor as regime-dependent short-h candidate.

verdicts.name: wdi_mom_90s
verdicts.note: Textbook retention pattern: huge OOS t at 15-60s, retention 0.38-0.46, passes only at 900s. tau1%/tau5% head legs look inverted vs the positive IC sign = sampling noise (40 rows/day); only tau10% agrees.

verdicts.name: dd_flow_300s
verdicts.note: Negative-IC continuation factor at 900s; head spread consistent with IC sign (both legs positive = OOS-week drift; bottom raw mean > top raw mean). Member of ti/dd flow-accumulator cluster (rho 0.89 with ti_accum_300s).

verdicts.name: rv_asym_300s

lessons: Verdicts are only valid relative to the eval-code version that produced them: the #141 split bug silently changed OOS composition for every historical screen. Any infrastructure fix touching splits/IC computation must trigger a full re-screen before new batches.

Retention >= 0.5 is the dominant killer of strong short-horizon signals: depth5_delta_60s, wdi_mom_90s, queue_refill_asym_300s show OOS |t| 3-11 at 15-60s yet fail retention 0.08-0.47 -> regime-dependent at short horizons, not noise. depth5_delta and wdi_mom pass at 900s instead. Do not re-propose raw clones at other windows; change normalization/window and expect horizon migration.
900s is currently the richest horizon (4 of 6 passes); 15-60s is carried by flow_divergence_300s alone. Never pre-exclude any horizon.

Head long/short reading convention: short_gross_bps = -mean(bottom); compare long_gross vs -short_gross; same-sign legs = OOS-week drift or time-of-day concentration; tau=1% legs are ~40 rows/day and noise-dominated at long horizons. Descriptive only, never gates.

Flow-accumulator redundancy: dd_flow_300s / ti_accum_300s / ti_ewm_state_300s form a rho 0.86-0.89 cluster; rv_asym_300s x ofi_accum_300s rho 0.750. Budget at most one representative per cluster per batch.
session_clock (time-of-day) is orthogonal to all market factors (max rho 0.252) and passes @60; it is a conditioning/detrending tool, not a standalone tradable factor.

polars 1.43 hazard: ewm_mean permanently contaminates state to NaN when input has leading nulls (engine warm-up), in both ignore_nulls modes. Use rolling_mean for warm-up-prone columns (enforced in iter-003 family B specs).
iopv premium momentum is regime-bound: strong IS, zero OOS. Premium-based factors need regime conditioning before re-submission (iter-003 family D).

admitted.name: depth5_delta_120s
admitted.mechanism: Slow depth momentum: the trailing-120s CHANGE in 5-level depth imbalance, integrating a full accumulation step of the deep book. Deep-book accumulation/distribution unfolds over minutes - meta-order slicing into passive limit orders, ETF creation/redemption inventory positioning - and a 60s delta sees only the first leg of such a build-up. The 120s window should match the 300-900s drift horizon where the parent depth5_delta_60s PASSED, testing whether longer integration improves horizon alignment and OOS stability of depth momentum, while differencing still strips the dead level state.

admitted.name: depth5_delta_30s
admitted.mechanism: Fast depth momentum: the trailing-30s CHANGE in 5-level depth imbalance (bid-ask)/(bid+ask), half the window of the eval-v2 PASS factor depth5_delta_60s. A 30s delta isolates the rapid reallocation of bid vs ask depth stock that precedes execution by seconds - informed traders pulling passive depth on the side they are about to trade against and stacking it on the side they favor - before the 60s window averages in older, already-priced flow. The parent showed strong short-horizon OOS t at 15-60s but missed IS-retention; a faster window may retain the short-horizon information that decays inside the 60s integration, at the cost of more event noise.

admitted.name: flow_divergence_120s
admitted.mechanism: Medium-horizon absorption divergence: between the fresh 60s variant and the champion's 300s window lies the 120s scale, where a stealth episode that started one or two minutes ago is still active but no longer noise-dominated. z(ofi) minus z(trade imbalance) over 120s measures whether book building over the last two minutes has systematically outrun (positive: passive bid accumulation beyond what trades justify -> up-continuation) or lagged (negative: hidden distribution) executed aggression. The three windowed variants (60/120/300s) triangulate which absorption bandwidth each prediction horizon rewards.

admitted.name: flow_divergence_60s
admitted.mechanism: Horizon-matched absorption/stealth divergence: the champion flow_divergence_300s compares z(ofi) and z(trade imbalance) over a 300s window -- appropriate for minute-scale absorption but over-smoothed for the 15-30s horizons where it also passes OOS. A 60s z window keeps the divergence FRESH: book building racing ahead of (or lagging) executed aggression within the last minute flags immediate stealth-limit activity whose price consequence is seconds away, not minutes. Same economic signal as the champion, bandwidth tuned to the short horizon.

admitted.name: flow_divergence_x_spread_z
admitted.mechanism: Stress-gated absorption: the flow_divergence signal (book flow minus trade flow) is strongest when it must EXPLAIN itself against stressed quoting. When spreads are wide (makers fearful, adverse selection high), a book that still builds one side beyond what executed aggression justifies is almost certainly informed stealth flow -> strong continuation at 15-60s. The same divergence under unusually tight, comfortable spreads may be routine queue noise. Multiplying by spread z gates the champion signal by the quoting state; the product is sign-symmetric and near-orthogonal to either parent.

admitted.name: last_mid_gap_ticks
admitted.mechanism: Instantaneous aggressor side: the mid is the quote midpoint, so where the last trade landed relative to it reveals who crossed. last > mid means the last print lifted the ask (a buyer was the aggressor, paying up); last < mid means it hit the bid (seller aggression); last == mid is a mid cross. The magnitude in ticks also scales with the half-spread, so wide-quote aggression reads larger. The aggressor side is the fastest directional microstructure signal on the panel -- it is determined by the very trade that moves price -- and a fresh aggressor imbalance predicts immediate (15-60s) continuation before the book re-equilibrates.

admitted.name: log_mid_ret_120s
admitted.mechanism: Two-minute signed mid momentum: bridges the fast 60s drift of the built-in and the slower accumulation state. A sustained 120s directional move reflects a multi-minute order-flow program (index rebalance, creation/redemption, informed accumulation) rather than a single burst, and such programs tend to persist (continuation into 60-300s) until their target size is filled. Conversely, a 120s move that has run far relative to recent vol flags overshoot and reversal. The 120s window decorrelates from the 60s window while still being fast enough for the short-horizon gate.

admitted.name: mid_day_range_pos
admitted.mechanism: Position within the intraday range encodes anchoring and stop-zone proximity. Traders anchor on the day's high/low and cluster stop orders just beyond them, so a mid near the top of the range (value ~1) sits next to a zone of resting buy-stops (breakout fuel) and overhead resistance, while a mid near the bottom (~0) sits next to sell-stops and support. Approaching an extreme predicts either continuation through the stop cluster or rejection off the level, and the exact rank position disambiguates where in the day's battle the current price sits -- information absent from pure momentum. Bounded [0,1], direction-free in level, ranked.

admitted.name: ofi_z_x_spread_z
admitted.mechanism: Stealth book-building under stress: OFI is dominated by limit-flow at the touch (placement/pull), and its predictive power exceeds signed trade volume (Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov 2014). When spreads are stressed wide, opportunistic liquidity providers retreat, so whoever is still BUILDING the book against the wide quote is likely informed -- passive queue accumulation precisely when passive quoting is most dangerous. Bid-side book growth under wide spreads predicts up-moves at 15-60s; the mirror for asks. Distinct from ti_z_x_spread_z: this conditions the PASSIVE/limit-order channel, which carries different (often leading) information than executed aggression.

admitted.name: oir_mom_60s
admitted.mechanism: Touch-level book-state momentum: the 60s change of the engine's top-of-book order imbalance ratio (oir). The touch queue can turn independently of the deeper weighted book - fast queue events like sweeps and refill bursts hit level 1 first - so oir momentum is a distinct derivative from wdi momentum: it measures queue-position pressure changing at the EXECUTING level. Rising oir = the bid queue gaining relative weight at the touch, which in queue-reactive price impact pushes the next ticks up; differencing strips the oir level state that market makers have already priced.

admitted.name: price_accel_60_180
admitted.mechanism: Momentum acceleration / deceleration: the difference between the trailing-60s and trailing-180s log-mid returns measures how the velocity of the current move is changing. A positive value means the last minute moved faster than the last three minutes -- the move is accelerating, the signature of fresh directional information still being incorporated (continuation likely). A negative value means the move is decelerating -- exhaustion, liquidity re-forming, reversal risk. Level momentum confounds direction with persistence; the first difference of momentum isolates persistence itself, which is what predicts the next 15-300s increment.

admitted.name: signed_rv_60s
admitted.mechanism: Directional concentration of variance over the last minute: the rolling sum of sign(ret)*ret^2 is up-RV minus down-RV in absolute (unnormalized) units. Positive means the quadratic variation of the last 60s is dominated by up moves (upside jumps), negative means down moves dominate (stop cascades / distressed selling). Unlike plain rv_60s it keeps the SIGN of which side the variance lives on, and unlike momentum it is variance-weighted, so a few large directional jumps dominate over many small ticks -- exactly the jump signature that carries. Being the 60s unnormalized cousin of the PASSed 900s rv_asym_300s, it targets the fast end of the same semivariance-asymmetry mechanism.

admitted.name: top_book_delta_120s
admitted.mechanism: Sustained touch-queue accumulation: the 120s delta of top-of-book quantity imbalance integrates REPEATED refill attempts rather than a single rebuild event. When the average touch imbalance drifts one-sided over two minutes, the queue is being strategically worked - iceberg-style replenishment keeping the displayed bid (or ask) heavy through successive consumptions, the passive leg of a meta-order establishing position. This slower touch trend is distinct from the 30s variant (single events) and from the deep depth5 deltas (levels 2-5), giving a third point in the top-vs-deep x fast-vs-slow decomposition of the live depth-momentum dimension.

admitted.name: wdi_accel_90s
admitted.mechanism: Second derivative of book state: how the 90s momentum of weighted depth imbalance is itself changing - the ACCELERATION of one-sided accumulation. Momentum says a build-up is under way; acceleration says whether it is intensifying or exhausting. Accelerating bid-side accumulation flags a fresh information episode still unfolding (continuation expected), while deceleration of a previously strong build-up marks exhaustion of the passive-flow source and precedes stall or reversion. Being a second difference, it is near-orthogonal to both the wdi level and the wdi momentum by construction, adding the turning-point dimension neither carries.

admitted.name: wdi_mom_180s
admitted.mechanism: Slow book-state momentum: the 180s change of the engine's weighted depth imbalance, integrating over intra-minute noise to measure the multi-minute ACCUMULATION REGIME of one-sided book build-up (meta-order passive legs, ETF basket arbitrage inventory). If depth momentum works at the 900s horizon because accumulation episodes persist, a longer delta should align the measurement with a fuller episode and improve OOS stability there; wdi's ~900s half-life means the 180s difference still removes the dead level state. Bracketing the PASS 90s window from above maps the horizon-response curve of book-state momentum.

admitted.name: wdi_mom_30s
admitted.mechanism: Fast book-state momentum: the 30s change of the engine's weighted depth imbalance (wdi), faster than the PASS wdi_mom_90s. wdi weights depth by price distance from the touch, so its fastest movements reflect near-touch re-pricing of imbalance; a 30s delta captures abrupt one-sided build-ups before the 90s window smooths them away. The parent showed strong short-horizon OOS t at 15-60s while failing IS-retention; this variant tests whether book-state momentum has a distinct fast component that carries at 15-60s, where the short-horizon reward for fast-moving state lives.
